theory: Qualify the claim that a horizontal line meets sine infinitely often: it holds for heights in $[-1,1]$, while heights outside that range have no intersections. Distinguish obtaining an inverse function from obtaining an inverse whose domain is the original function's full range: one-to-one restrictions can have smaller ranges, so full-range coverage is an additional requirement rather than a necessary condition for every inverse.
